summary:
Today a ship shows its damage only through smoke (below half hull) and the bars on its tag. Every material is shared: raiderArt clones one set per colour scheme, and raiderShip's body.clone() shares geometry and materials. So nothing can differ from one raider to the next, and nothing on the models moves except the sway, the rudder, sail ripple, pennants, glows and embers.

The cheapest robust path has three parts:
- **Per-ship material clones that share their compiled shaders.** Each clone keeps the same customProgramCacheKey and its onBeforeCompile reads the ship's own uniforms. I tested this in headless Chromium (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/7e489355-d0a0-5ded-9e0b-bc551db36d16/scratchpad/survey/ships-alive/probe.mjs). Dressing a full Brig's hull, sails and crystals took the hangar from 19 to 22 programs. Dressing a second copy kept it at 22.
- **One uniform set per ship.**
- **One vec4 'rig' vertex attribute, written at build time.** It goes only on the small batches (wood, rope, canvas, crystal, gem, parts, and a new rigMetal key), never on brass or bronze, which hold 40,000 to 50,000 triangles at full. With it, wings fold, lids swing and guns run out in the vertex shader with no new triangles.

The prototype pictures read well from the game's high camera behind the ship:
- brig-wear-behind.png: holed, charred sails
- brig-wear.png: scorched, holed hull
- brig-wear-close.png: crazed crystals

A pitfall the probe found: one copy of the ship still carried the full-detail ship's PointLights, and it recompiled every lit shader (22 to 32 programs). Never add or remove a light mid-voyage.

Top recommendation, in order:
1. The dress/looks core with holed sails, scorched hull and dying crystals. All of it is fragment-shader work: no triangles, no draw calls, and it works at middle and far.
2. Show it in the ships demo's "Battered" button so Chris can see it on his phone.
3. Wings that fold with the sail setting, and the aether wakes. These give the biggest sense of life and speed.
4. Fire, gun crews, and the three special looks (captain, treasure ship, Man-o'-war).

Note: the src/game files are being edited by the build workflow right now. Anchors there are by function name. src/ship line numbers are stable (unchanged since 11:40).
architecture:
ONE SHARED CORE ("dress" + "looks"), then features plug in.

1) src/ship/dress.js (new, generic, used by the game and the hangar)
- makeLook() returns U, one uniform set per ship:
  - uWTime: ONE object shared by every ship, set once a frame in main.js tick and the hangar's frame()
  - uScar: Float32Array(24), hull scars as body-space xyz plus radius
  - uHeat: Float32Array(6)
  - uHole: Float32Array(24), sail holes as xyz plus radius; a negative radius means patched
  - uWear: vec4 (grime, fray, flap, unused)
  - uCrys: Float32Array(8), brightness per crystal cluster
  - uCrack: Float32Array(8)
  - uSpark: float, the sputter multiplier, worked out on the CPU
  - uGun: vec4 (open port, open starboard, run port, run starboard)
  - uFireT: vec4 (time of the last volley: port, starboard, bow, stern)
  - uReload: vec4
  - uFold: vec2 (fold, flutter)
  - uWind: vec2 (speed fraction, strike)
  - uMark: float
  That is under 30 uniform vectors.
- dress(body, M, U) walks the body and swaps each mesh's material, by mesh name, for a per-ship clone:
  - hull, plates and deck use the 'hull-wear' chunk; their feature flags match, so they share one program
  - wood: 'wood-rig'
  - canvas: 'sail-wear'
  - rope: 'rope-rig'
  - crystal: 'crystal-rig'
  - rigMetal: 'metal-rig'
  - gem: 'gem-wear'
  - parts: 'parts-rig'
  - flag: 'flag-wind'
  It also clones the 'glow' and 'embers' ShaderMaterials.
- Pitfalls:
  - Material.clone() deep-copies userData through JSON, so U must be attached after cloning (clone.userData.U = U).
  - onBeforeCompile must be a plain function that reads this.userData.U. three r186 calls material.onBeforeCompile(parameters, renderer) once per material, and acquireProgram reuses the program by key.
  - brass, bronze, band and dark stay shared and are not dressed.
- GLSL chunks live there as strings:
  - WEAR_NOISE: Inigo Quilez's hash without sin, plus a 3D value noise; stable at mediump
  - RIG_VERTEX: decodes 'rig', moves the vertex and its normal, and writes the varyings vLocal = position, vRig and vEdge
  - HULL_WEAR_FRAG: injected after #include <map_fragment> and after <emissivemap_fragment>
  - SAIL_WEAR_FRAG
  - GEM_WEAR_FRAG
  - CANVAS ripple and FLAG wave, moved from materials.js L104-115 and driven by U.uWTime
- Export foldPoint(p, rig, fold) and gunOffset(...) so CPU code (hit zones, wingtip trails, tests) agrees exactly with the GPU.

2) Build-time tags: src/ship/kit.js Batch
- Add 'rig' to the attribute allowlist (L40) and to the fill sizes (L54: rig → 4).
- New fields: this.tag (a constant [kind, a, b, c]) and this.tagFn((x, y, z) => [...]). Batch.add writes a Float32 'rig' when either is set.
- Batch.build (L46-58) already fills an attribute only within keys that have it, so only tagged keys carry rig.
- Encoding of kind:
  - 0: static
  - 1: wing [1, side*(1+w), mastZ, edge]
  - 2: lid [2, hingeX, hingeY, delay]
  - 3: port gun [3, side*D, delay, 0]
  - 4: chaser [4, axis, delay, dist]
  - 5: crystal cluster [5, clusterIndex, 0, 0]
- New key 'rigMetal': one MeshStandardMaterial with vertexColors, metalness 0.87 and roughness 0.35. The bronze (0xa06a2e) or brass (0xd9a743) of each piece is baked into 'color'. It holds the moving metal: port-gun barrels and rings, lid trims, chaser bands and yard spikes. This keeps 'brass' (40,604 triangles on the full Brig) and 'bronze' (22,338) untagged.
- Measured small keys on the full Brig: wood 3,812, rope 3,112, canvas 1,800, crystal 744, gem 480 and parts 300 triangles. rig costs about 0.7 MB of vertex memory on a full ship and about 0.2 MB per raider class at middle. That memory is per template, not per raider, because raiders share geometry.

3) src/game/looks.js (new): the live state behind each U, with no allocation per frame (scratch vectors only)
- attach(ship, flyer, {raider, captain, id}): called in main.js sail() and raiders.spawn
- hit(ship, part, worldAt, damage, size, idx):
  - called from main.js hitTest, both branches
  - local point = worldAt × the inverse of body.matrixWorld
  - size is the bolt's K.size
  - idx is the crystal or sail box from firstHit
- fired(ship, battery, reload): called from guns.js makeGunnery.fire right after ready[b] = reload(b), through a ship.looks hook, so player and raiders both work untouched
- update(dt, time): called once from main.js tick after raiders.update. It eases lid, run and fold, heat, sputter, list and trim, and writes U.
- repair(k): called from waves() next to player.repair
- reset(ship): called on sail() and when entering port
- If fx-core's event bus from survey1-feel gets built, looks subscribes to its 'hit' and 'volley' events instead.

4) Raiders: raiders.js
- raiderShip(T) keeps body.clone() and then calls dress(clone, arts.M, makeLook()) per raider, on its mid and far bodies alike.
- Template bodies are never shown and stay undressed.
- raiderShip.update and detail drive the raider's own glow and ember clones.
- Template-level looks (captain, treasure ship, Man-o'-war) are set in raiderArt and template(), which cost nothing at runtime.

5) damage.js
- firstHit's tryBox also records bestIdx and returns idx (which crystal column or which mast's sails).
- hitZones builds the sail boxes as the union of the canvas at fold 0 and fold 1, using foldPoint.
- buildShip returns wings: [{mast, side, A, B, C}], pushed from parts.js masts() the way glows are. A sail hit (which is only a box hit) is projected onto the nearest wing triangle, so the hole lands on the canvas.

6) No hitches
- No new programs appear at runtime: every dressed variant is the same program for player and raiders, and the probe showed no new programs for a second dressed ship.
- In sail(), after scene.add(ship.root), call renderer.compileAsync(scene, camera).
- Keep building captain templates ahead with raiders.prepare, which the build workflow already added.
- Never add or remove PointLights during a voyage.
- Give the middle/far swap hysteresis in raiders.update: go far below 0.055, middle above 0.065 (today a single 0.06 threshold).

7) Test hooks
- window.__game.looks: state and gunOffset
- window.__game.wakes.stats() and window.__game.flames.count
- window.__hangar.wear(preset) and window.__hangar.rig({fold, open})

8) Docs to keep in step
- docs/game.md: the Hull bullet (~L136: "below a quarter it burns too") and the raiders section
- docs/ships.md: the raiders' colours (L39) and what each level of detail shows (L130-143)
- tools/check.mjs: BUDGET stays { full 80-125k, middle 10-50k, far 1-8k }

proposals.title: Holed and tattered sails (and the shared dress/looks core)
proposals.chris_sees: Every shot that hits a sail punches a ragged hole with brown, scorched edges, right where it hit, and the hole grows if it is hit again. Below about 60% on the sails bar, the sails' loose edges start to fray into tatters and the canvas flaps harder. At zero sails they are rags. It happens to his own ship too, where the sails are the biggest thing on screen from the camera behind. On raiders far off, the tatters change their outline, so he can tell a raider has lost her sails without reading her tag.
proposals.why: It puts the sails bar on the ship itself. The prototype (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/7e489355-d0a0-5ded-9e0b-bc551db36d16/scratchpad/survey/ships-alive/brig-wear-behind.png) shows the holes reading clearly from a game-like camera. It also builds the core every later look reuses.
proposals.how:
1. **Core:** build src/ship/dress.js and src/game/looks.js as in the architecture. In buildShip (src/ship/build.js L114) call dress(body, art.M, makeLook()) and return { U, looks hook }. In raiders.js raiderShip (L75) dress each clone with its own U.
2. **Edge value:** in parts.js sail() (L398-420), push wc (the weight of corner C, the yard root) per vertex. It goes into rig.w, with rig = [1, ±2, M.z, wc] when wings are tagged, or [0, 0, 0, wc] otherwise. It is 0 along the free edge A–B and 1 at the yard root.
3. **SAIL_WEAR_FRAG,** after #include <map_fragment> in the dressed canvas:
   - wn = 0.6·noise(vLocal·3.1) + 0.4·noise(vLocal·9)
   - for each of 6 holes: d = |vLocal − h.xyz| / h.w + (wn − 0.5)·0.8; discard if d < 0.5; char = max(char, 1 − smoothstep(0.5, 0.78, d))
   - fray: discard if vEdge < uWear.y·(0.35 + 0.9·wn)
   - diffuseColor.rgb *= mix(1, 0.1, char)
   - after <emissivemap_fragment>: totalEmissiveRadiance *= 1 − char
   - skip the loop when no hole is set: if (uHole[0].w == 0.0)
4. **Vertex:** the ripple from materials.js L106 is reused, with its amplitude × uWear.z.
5. **looks.hit(part 'sails'):**
   - Project the hit onto the canvas: intersect the bolt's local ray with that mast's wing triangles (ship.wings) and take the first barycentric hit; otherwise take the nearest point on the nearest wing.
   - Radius r = 1.0 m × K.size (visible hole about 0.5 m chaser, 0.68 m broadside).
   - Merge with a hole within 1.2·r: r = min(0.4 × tier span, hypot(r, r0)). Otherwise add one, or replace the smallest of the 6.
6. **looks.update, each frame:**
   - uWear.y (fray) = 0.55·smoothstep(0.6, 0, sails fraction)
   - uWear.z (flap) = 1 + 2.5·(1 − sails fraction)
7. In main.js tick, replace the global art.M.canvas.userData.time update with U.uWTime.
proposals.phone_cost:
- No new triangles or draw calls, and no new textures.
- One program variant ('sail-wear') replaces today's 'sail-ripple', and every ship shares it (checked: 22 programs before and after dressing a second ship).
- About 100 fragment operations per sail pixel, only once a ship has holes or fray: the loop is skipped while uHole[0].w is 0.
- discard only on the canvas program, which is a small share of the screen.
- Each raider gets 10 to 12 material clones (kilobytes), made once at spawn.
- Up close the holes carry the message; at 300 m and more, the fray carries it.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs (game), using a frozen Brig raider spawned 200 m abeam (__game.raiders.spawn):
- Call __game.looks.hit(r.ship, 'sails', a point on a wing, 55, 1.35). Assert r.ship.U.uHole.value[3] > 0, and that the hole centre lies within 0.3 m of a wing triangle's plane.
- Note __game.renderer.info.programs.length, spawn a second Brig, render one frame, and assert the count is unchanged.
- Drop r.f.health.sails to 20% and step(0.2); assert uWear.y > 0.3.
- Pixel test: render a 320×240 close-up before and after the hits and read it back with readPixels; require at least 2% of pixels changed.

proposals.title: Scorched, holed planks that glow with embers, and a wounded ship that lists
proposals.chris_sees: Each hit on the hull leaves a blackened scorch mark with a dark hole and a ring of splintered pale wood, exactly where it struck. The mark glows with embers for a few seconds, then smoulders. As the hull bar drops, the whole hull gets sooty and streaked. A badly holed ship leans over toward the side that took the hits. His own deck and stern show it too.
proposals.why: It turns the hull bar into something he can see, and makes every hit leave a mark that stays. In the prototype (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/7e489355-d0a0-5ded-9e0b-bc551db36d16/scratchpad/survey/ships-alive/brig-wear.png) the scorches read at 27 m.
proposals.how:
1. **HULL_WEAR_FRAG** in the dressed hull, plates and deck clones (one shared 'hull-wear' program). After <map_fragment>:
   - wn = 0.65·noise(vLocal·2.3) + 0.35·noise(vLocal·6.1)
   - for each of 6 scars: d = |vLocal − s.xyz| / s.w + (wn − 0.5)·0.9
     - soot = max(soot, 1 − smoothstep(0.55, 2.1, d))
     - hole = 1 − smoothstep(0.3, 0.36, d)
     - rim = band 0.36–0.5
     - ember = uHeat[i]·(1 − smoothstep(0.3, 1.0, d))
   - soot = max(soot, uWear.x·smoothstep(0.5, 0.85, wn)): grime patches
   - diffuse *= mix(1, 0.15, soot); rim mixes toward (0.45, 0.3, 0.18) at 0.7; hole sets diffuse to (0.01, 0.007, 0.005)
2. **After <emissivemap_fragment>:**
   - totalEmissiveRadiance *= 1 − 0.9·max(soot, hole): the planks' own glow goes out
   - add (1.0, 0.22, 0.04)·ember·(0.65 + 0.35·sin(9t + 25·wn))·1.4
   - The prototype's 2.2× brighter ember read as brass, so use this redder, dimmer one.
3. **looks.hit(part 'hull'):**
   - firstHit's point is already within 0.2 m of the hull surface (it steps 0.2 m in damage.js).
   - r = 1.4 m × K.size, so the soot reaches about 3 m and the hole core is about 0.45 m.
   - Merge with a scar within 1.6·r (grow r up to 3 m); otherwise replace the coolest, smallest of 6.
   - heat = 1, decaying at 1/5 per second to a floor of 0.15.
4. **Grime:** uWear.x = smoothstep(0.85, 0.15, hull fraction).
5. **List:**
   - target = clamp(Σ(x_i·r_i) / Σ r_i / half-beam, −1, 1)·(1 − hull fraction)·0.07 rad (cap 0.04 for the player, so the guns' tilt range barely changes)
   - eased at 1/s and passed as opts.list to ship.update
   - shipMotion (build.js L101-112) adds it to body.rotation.z at L107
   - flight.js passes opts through at the update and sink calls
   - Hit zones follow, because body.matrixWorld is used.
6. Hits on the deck from above show on the deck, because deck shares the chunk.
7. These scar positions are the same list the earlier battle-scars proposal uses for smoke, so emit smoke from them (effects.js smokeFrom).
proposals.phone_cost:
- No triangles or draw calls.
- About 160 fragment operations per hull pixel (two noise octaves and a 6-step loop), only after the first hit: a uniform check skips it while pristine. A full ship's hull is about 15-25% of a phone screen, so roughly 1-2% of a mid-range GPU.
- The list is one value per ship.
- Middle and far raiders get the same look for the same cost per pixel, so detail switches don't make it pop.
proposals.test:
- Frozen Frigate: looks.hit(..., 'hull', the world point of hull.at(-3, 0.3, 1), 55, 1.35). Assert U.uScar.value[3] ≈ 1.89 and U.uHeat.value[0] == 1. After step(5), heat is below 0.3.
- Set hull to 20% with scars on +x: after step(3), |ship.body.rotation.z − sway| > 0.03 and its sign matches the side.
- Pixel diff of a side close-up, before and after: more than 2% changed.
- The program count does not change when a second raider of the class spawns.

proposals.title: Crystals that dim where hit, craze with cracks and sputter as they fail
proposals.chris_sees: The crystals that get hit dim first. Then white cracks spread across them, and the furnace windows under them go darker. Once the crystals bar falls below a third, all the ship's crystals sputter and flicker together, the sparks drifting off them thin out, and the deck lights falter. On his own ship this is right in front of the camera, on the deck.
proposals.why: The crystals bar is the one that sinks a ship, and right now nothing on the model shows it. The glows are big and bright, so dimming reads even at 1 km. The prototype's cracks are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/7e489355-d0a0-5ded-9e0b-bc551db36d16/scratchpad/survey/ships-alive/brig-wear-close.png.
proposals.how:
1. **Tag each cluster:** in parts.js clusters() (L236-296), set batch.tag = [5, clusterIndex, 0, 0] while making each cluster's pieces (the furnace 'parts' column at L249, the 'gem' crystals at L289), then clear it.
2. **Glow points** (build.js glowPoints, L67-99):
   - add a 'group' attribute: clusterIndex + 1 for the glows pushed at parts.js L290, L292 and L294; 0 for lanterns and guns
   - add uniforms uCrys[8] and uSpark; in the vertex shader: if (group > 0.5) k *= uCrys[int(group) − 1]·uSpark
   - This replaces the single uDim from the earlier battle-scars proposal with one value per cluster.
3. **Embers** (emberPoints, L36-64): add the same group attribute, and set gl_PointSize = 0 when hash(seed·7.7) > uCrys[g], so the sparks thin out.
4. **GEM_WEAR_FRAG:**
   - in the vertex shader, read vCrys and vCrack from the arrays by rig.y; no dynamic indexing in the fragment shader
   - line = 1 − smoothstep(0, 0.045, |noise(vLocal·5) − 0.5|)
   - emissive *= vCrys·uSpark·(1 − 0.85·line·vCrack)
   - diffuse *= 1 − 0.8·line·vCrack
   - the cracks flash violet-white (0.75, 0.55, 1) when sputtering
   - move today's global pulse (main.js tick: art.M.gem.emissiveIntensity = 0.55 + 0.09·sin(2.4t), also hangar.js L301) into the shader using uWTime
5. **Furnace** (dressed 'parts'): emissive *= mix(1, vCrys·uSpark, isCluster).
6. **Lights** (build.js update L159-163): lamp intensity × uCrys[i]·uSpark. There is one lamp per cluster, in the same order.
7. **looks:**
   - crystal hits use firstHit's idx (damage.js tryBox records bestIdx)
   - d_i += damage; col_i = 1 − d_i / (full crystals / number of clusters)
   - uCrys_i = 0.2 + 0.8·col_i; uCrack_i = smoothstep(0.75, 0.25, col_i)
   - uSpark, worked out on the CPU so gems, glows, embers and lamps flicker together: if crystals fraction < 0.35, it is 1 when noise(t·11) > 0.35 and 0.25 otherwise
   - repair scales every d_i by D_new / D_old
   - when a ship goes down for 'crystals', all uCrys fall to 0 over 2 s
proposals.phone_cost:
- No triangles or draw calls.
- The glows and embers change in the vertex shader only: a handful of operations per point.
- The gem fragment work covers a tiny area.
- One uniform array per ship.
proposals.test:
- Frozen Frigate, 3 clusters: hit the crystals box of cluster 0 with 60% of its share. Assert U.uCrys[0] < 0.6, uCrys[1] and uCrys[2] == 1, and uCrack[0] > 0.
- Take total crystals below 35% and step(2): uSpark takes both 1 and 0.25 within the sampled frames.
- Repair: in the 'choose' state, step(20) and assert uCrys[0] rises.
- The full ship's lamp intensity is below 50% of nominal for a dimmed cluster.

proposals.title: Wing sails that fold back and spread with the sail setting; pennants that answer speed
proposals.chris_sees: When he takes in sail (S), his wing sails sweep back along the hull like a bird folding its wings. When he sets more sail (W), they spread wide, and a Surge snaps them fully open with a shiver. Raiders spread their wings to chase and half-fold them when they slow to bring a broadside round. The pennants stream out straight at speed and hang limp when the ship is slow. A ship going down folds its wings.
proposals.why: The sails fill the screen from the camera behind, so this is the most visible way to make the ship look alive. It turns the sail control into something he can see, and it reads as speed.
proposals.how:
1. **Tag the wing pieces** in parts.js masts() (L327-346) with [1, side·(1 + w), M.z, edge], w = 1 for parts that move rigidly:
   - the yard lathe (L334, wood)
   - the yard spike (L335): moves into rigMetal
   - the sail (L340, canvas)
   - the leech rope [A, tip] (L341, rigid)
   - the sheet [tip, rail] (L344): ropes become [a, b, tag]; in the tube loop (L372-376) a tagFn gives w = 1 − t along the rope, so the rail end stays put
2. **RIG_VERTEX, kind 1:**
   - θ = sign(rig.y)·(0.6·uFold.x − 0.06·surge + 0.012·sin(18t)·uFold.y)
   - about the vertical line through (0, ·, M.z): x' = x·cosθ + (z − M.z)·sinθ; z' = M.z − x·sinθ + (z − M.z)·cosθ
   - droop: y' = y − 0.12·uFold.x·|x|
   - p = mix(p, p', |rig.y| − 1); rotate the normal by θ too
   - Keep θmax at 0.6 rad (34°), so the Frigate's fore wings stay clear of the mainmast's (8.25 m apart).
3. **Fold value:**
   - fold = clamp(1 − sail, 0, 1), eased at 2/s; a Surge gives −0.1 and flutter 1
   - port: 0, spread for show
   - going down: rises to 1 over 2 s
   - raiders get it from f.sail (their sailTo is 0.6-1)
   - Pass sail, speed fraction and surge from flight.js (the ship.update call at the end of s.update) through build.js update into U.
4. **Flag** (materials.js L110-115, moved to dress.js):
   - droop = billow²·0.35·(1.4 − uWind.x)
   - flap frequency × (0.7 + 0.6·uWind.x)
5. **Hit zones** (damage.js hitZones): each mast's sail box is the union of the canvas vertices at fold 0 and fold 1 (CPU foldPoint), so folded sails still take hits.
6. If the shadow fix (F05) lands, give the player's canvas and wood meshes a customDepthMaterial with RIG_VERTEX.
7. **Far level:** the canvas and wood are tagged too (tiny); the spike stays static, since it's sub-pixel there.
proposals.phone_cost:
- No triangles.
- No draw calls beyond rigMetal's +1, shared with gun-crews.
- About 20 vertex operations on wood, canvas and rope only: about 8,000 vertices on a middle Brig, 25,000 on a full one.
- rig vertex memory as in the architecture (about 0.7 MB on a full ship).
- One uniform per ship.
proposals.test:
- __game.fly('frigate'); step(3, {sail: -1}): player.ship.U.uFold.value.x > 0.9. Then step(3, {sail: 1}): < 0.1.
- foldPoint of a known yard tip at fold 1 lies at least 3 m further aft than at fold 0.
- A frozen raider at sail 0.75 has fold about 0.25.
- A bolt fired through the centre of a fully folded wing (firstHit) returns 'sails'.
- Hangar picture with 'Sails: furled' (see hangar-battle-worn).

proposals.title: Glowing aether wakes behind every ship, and vapour trails off the wingtips
proposals.chris_sees: A soft, shimmering ribbon of stirred-up Aether streams behind every ship from under her stern, longer and brighter the faster she flies. His is gold and sweeps away beneath the camera. Raiders' are red, so a raider far off shows as a red streak about twice her own length. A captain's is crimson-violet and a treasure ship's glitters gold. In hard turns, dives and a Surge, thin white vapour trails peel off his wingtips.
proposals.why: It gives a sense of speed without camera tricks, makes the sky feel busy, and shows where raiders are and which way they are heading at ranges where the far model is about 17 pixels long. ships.md already says the sails catch the Aether.
proposals.how:
1. **New src/game/wakes.js:** makeWakes(scene, {maxTrails: 24, points: touch ? 14 : 22, every: 0.07}).
   - Preallocated Float32Arrays, 2 vertices per point:
     - position: the centre point
     - tan: a vec3, the CPU tangent (previous point − next point)
     - meta: vec2 (side ±1, age 0..1)
     - col: vec4 (rgb, intensity)
   - One prebuilt index buffer (6 per segment).
   - Upload only the used range (attribute.updateRanges) and set the draw range; this avoids the whole-buffer uploads of bug F19.
2. **attach(flyer, {color, kind}):**
   - Keel trail emitter: (0, keel(zs + 0.1L) + 0.2, zs + 0.1L) in body space, width 0.09·L.
   - Player, and raiders at middle detail: two vapour trails at the outermost top-tier yard tips, run through dress.js foldPoint, width 0.25 m.
   - Called from main.js sail() and raiders.spawn (pass an onSpawn hook to makeRaiders).
   - Trails whose owner is gone fade out over 1 s.
3. **update(dt, camera), once a frame in tick after raiders.update and placeCamera:**
   - Every 0.07 s push the emitter's world point (body.localToWorld into a scratch vector) into the trail's ring; always rewrite the head point, so the trail never gaps.
   - Intensity:
     - aether: 0.25 + 0.75·(speed / vmax)^1.5, ×1.8 in a Surge, 0 once down
     - vapour: eased toward 0.35 while speed > 0.85·vmax, |turn| > 0.6 or surging, otherwise 0
4. **ShaderMaterial,** additive, depthWrite false, renderOrder 3:
   - vertex: side vector = normalize(cross(tan, cameraPosition − position)); halfW = max(w·(0.35 + 0.65·(1 − age)), uMinPx·(−mv.z) / uScale), where uScale is camera.userData.pixelScale and uMinPx is 1.6 on a phone, 2 on a laptop
   - fragment: a = (1 − age)^1.6·(1 − side²)·intensity·(0.75 + 0.25·sin(age·40 − 9t))
   - glitter kind: add step(0.985, hash(floor(age·60), floor(t·12)))·2
5. **Colours:**
   - player: 0xffc860
   - raider: 0xff5a3a
   - captain: 0xff3070
   - Galleon: 0xffd56a with glitter
   - Man-o'-war: 0xff8a2a at 1.4× width
   - vapour: 0xf4f8ff
6. This replaces the vapour puffs in step 4 of the earlier surge-speed proposal (no smoke puffs needed). Clear the wakes in sail() and endVoyage.
proposals.phone_cost:
- 1 draw call for every ship together.
- At most 24 × 14 × 2 = 672 vertices on a phone (1,056 on a laptop); about 15-25 KB uploaded a frame.
- A few hundred tangent calculations on the CPU, with no allocation.
- The additive fill is thin ribbons.
- No textures.
proposals.test:
- __game.wakes.stats() returns { trails, points }: after fly('brig') and step(2, {sail: 1}), there is 1 + the number of raiders, and the player's keel trail's head-to-tail distance is over 0.8 × speed × 1.3 s.
- A frozen raider placed 1.6 km off still has a trail with intensity above 0.2 once it flies.
- renderer.info.render.calls with wakes visible minus with wakes hidden is exactly 1.
- No garbage: steady heap in a 10 s step.

proposals.title: A 'Battered' button in the ships demo, so Chris can see the scars on his phone
proposals.chris_sees:
The ships demo gets a new row of buttons:
- **Ship:** New / Battered / Wrecked. Battered shows scorched planks with holes, holed sails and cracked, dimmer crystals. Wrecked shows tattered sails, burning patches and crystals sputtering.
- **Sails:** Spread / Half / Furled
- **Guns:** Run in / Run out

He can turn any ship round and zoom in on the damage at full, middle or far detail.
proposals.why: Every step should end with something Chris can open on his phone. The demo is the clearest place to judge the looks one at a time, and it makes good regression pictures for the check.
proposals.how:
1. **demos/hangar.html:** add a .seg group #wear with buttons data-wear='new|battered|wrecked', and #rigs with data-sails and data-guns. They copy the #levels markup at L110-113 and wrap on a phone.
2. **src/demo/hangar.js:**
   - getShip (L142-146) dresses each built ship with its own U.
   - frame() (L289-305) sets the shared uWTime and calls ship.update(dt, {sail, guns}).
   - wearPreset(ship, name) fills U deterministically:
     - battered: 4 scars at hull.at(z, t, ±1) for z at 25/45/60/80% of the length and t 0.2-0.5, r 1.4; 3 sail holes at wing triangle centroids, r 1.2; uCrys 0.55 with crack 0.6 on one cluster; grime 0.4; fray 0.15
     - wrecked: 6 scars with heat 1, fray 0.5, uCrys 0.25, uSpark sputtering, and the flames from hull-fire if built
3. Add __hangar.wear(name) and __hangar.rig({fold, open}) to the hooks at L309-315.
4. **tools/closeups.mjs:** add a 'worn' argument that shoots each preset.
5. Publish dist/hangar.artifact.html to the ships demo link as CLAUDE.md says.
proposals.phone_cost: Same as the dressing itself: no triangles, and the draw calls only change when rigMetal comes with gun-crews (+1). The buttons are HTML.
proposals.test:
In the check.mjs hangar section, for laptop and phone:
- Screenshot New, Battered and Wrecked.
- Assert a pixel difference of more than 3% between New and Battered (screenshot buffers compared in node).
- Assert the triangle table is unchanged within BUDGET.
- Assert __hangar.wear('battered') sets U.uScar.value[3] > 0.

proposals.title: Real flames licking from the worst holes below a quarter hull, streaming aft
proposals.chris_sees: Below a quarter on the hull bar, flames burst from the ship's two worst wounds, then three or four as she gets closer to sinking. They flicker, sway and stream back along the hull as she flies, and the scorched planks around them glow. A ship going down for good burns all along her holes. His own ship burns the same way when he is in trouble.
proposals.why: docs/game.md already says a ship below a quarter "burns too", but today that is only orange sparks (effects.js smokeFrom). Real flames are the clearest warning there is, for him and about raiders.
proposals.how:
1. **New makeFlames(scene, max = touch ? 16 : 28)** in src/game/effects.js:
   - InstancedBufferGeometry from PlaneGeometry(1, 1, 1, 4).translate(0, 0.5, 0)
   - instanced attributes, DynamicDrawUsage: iPos vec3, iSize vec2, iSeed, iHeat, iLean vec3
   - ShaderMaterial: additive, depthWrite false, toneMapped false, renderOrder 3
2. **Vertex:** a billboard that turns round the upright only.
   - right = normalize(cross(up, cameraPosition − iPos)); y = position.y
   - sway = sin(7t + 13·seed + 3y)·0.12·y²
   - world = iPos + right·position.x·iSize.x·(1 − 0.6y) + up·y·iSize.y + (right·sway + iLean·y²)·iSize.y
3. **Fragment:**
   - n = 2D value noise of uv·(3, 5) − (0, 3.5t + seed)
   - shape = smoothstep(0.5, 0, |u − 0.5|·(1.2 + 1.5v) + 0.35·n·v)·smoothstep(1, 0.55, v + 0.3n)
   - colour = mix((1, 0.9, 0.55), (1, 0.3, 0.05), v + 0.2n)·iHeat
4. **Feeding, in looks.update:**
   - for each ship with hull fraction < 0.25, or down by 'hull', its 2 hottest scars burn (3 below 0.12, all of them when down); their uHeat is pinned at 1
   - per flame:
     - iPos = body.localToWorld(scar + 0.25 m along the hull normal); the normal is hull.normal(z, tAt(z, y), sign x)
     - iSize = (0.9, 2.2)·clamp(L/25, 0.6, 1.8)
     - iLean = −velocity·0.025, clamped to 1.5 m
   - write into the instance arrays with no allocation
5. smokeFrom (effects.js) emits from the flame tips instead of a random spot, and drops its fire sparks above burning 0.5 (keep a few embers).
6. **No lights:** the hull's ember glow (scorched-holed-hull) fakes the firelight.
proposals.phone_cost:
- 1 draw call for the whole sky.
- At most 16 instances (8 triangles each) on a phone.
- The flames are small additive quads.
- Two noise lookups per flame pixel.
- About 100 floats written a frame.
proposals.test:
- Frozen Brig: give it scars with looks.hit, then r.f.hit('hull', 0.8·full). After step(0.2), __game.flames.count >= 2, and every flame's iPos is within 1.2 m of the hull.
- Repair to 60% and step(0.2): count is 0.
- renderer.info.render.calls rises by exactly 1 when the first flame appears.

proposals.title: Gun crews: lids swing open, guns run out, kick back on firing and run out again when reloaded
proposals.chris_sees: When a wave appears, the gun-port lids down his ship's sides fly open from bow to stern and the guns roll out. Between waves the crew closes them. When a side fires, its guns jump back and stay in while they reload, then roll out again when they are ready, just as the reload bar fills. His bow and stern guns visibly kick. A raider's lids fly open and her guns run out on the side facing him a moment before her broadside, so he can see it coming.
proposals.why: It makes ship-to-ship fighting feel like the age of sail. The guns' state shows the reload clock on the model. On raiders the lids give a warning he can read, alongside the red port glow from the earlier raider-broadside-warning proposal. The camera looks at a raider's facing side, so this is where it shows most.
proposals.how:
1. **Lids** in parts.js gunPort (L177-202), built closed:
   - lh = h + 2b, so the closed lid covers the port
   - the hinge moves out to z = d + 0.004
   - no 'open' rotation is baked in
   - tag = [2, hingeX, hingeY, rank·0.06], with the hinge at m·(0, h/2 + b, d) in body space
   - hull.normal ignores the hull's curve along its length (hull.js L33-37), so every hinge axis is exactly ±z and every barrel axis exactly ±x: no axis needs storing
   - middle level: LEVELS.middle.portLids = 'board' (the board only, 12 triangles, no trims)
2. **Port guns:** the barrel lathe (L189) and its ring (L190) move to key 'rigMetal' (bronze or brass in the colour attribute), and the crystal tip (L191) stays in 'crystal'. All tagged [3, side·(0.83h + 0.15), delay, 0].
3. **Chasers** (longGun, L141-174): the barrel (wood), bands and muzzle (rigMetal), and the chamber and point (crystal) are tagged [4, axis (+1 bow, −1 stern, ±2 swivel), delay, 0.25·len]. The swivel base and post stay static.
4. **RIG_VERTEX:**
   - **Lid:** a = smoothstep(delay, delay + 0.35, uGun.(side)). Rotate about the z-parallel line through (hx, hy) by side·2.25·a; check the sign so a = 1 matches today's baked lid at open = −2.25.
   - **Gun:** x −= side·D·(1 − run_side) + side·kick.
     - kick(u), with u = t − uFireT.side − delay: rises to 0.45·L in 0.06 s, holds until 0.7·uReload.side, then smoothsteps back to 0 by uReload.
   - **Chaser:** the same kick along its axis.
5. **State, in build.js update via opts.guns, or looks:**
   - player: lids open while W.state === 'fight' (the 'clear for action' ripple at the wave banner); closed in calm, choose and port
   - run = 1 once the lid is past 0.85
   - raiders: open within 1,200 m of the Captain, or when a broadside charge starts if that proposal is built
   - makeGunnery.fire calls ship.looks?.fired(b, reload), setting uFireT[b] = time and uReload[b] = reload
6. **Ripple timing:** the delays use one helper, portRank(R, z), sorting bow first and shared with the ripple-broadsides g.delay (step min(0.055, 0.55 / (n − 1))). If the ripple is not built, the delay step is 0.
proposals.phone_cost:
- +1 draw call per ship at full and middle ('rigMetal'), none at far.
- Triangles:
  - full: unchanged, since the lids, barrels and rings only change key
  - middle, adding 12 per port: Cutter +72, Brig +144, Frigate +240, Galleon +384, Man-o'-war +576 (46,926 → 47,502, inside the 50,000 middle budget)
- About 20 vertex operations on the small rig batches.
- Two vec4 uniforms per ship.
proposals.test:
- The hangar triangle table stays within BUDGET, and its draw calls are 18 at full and middle.
- Hangar: __hangar.rig({open: 1}) against today's picture of open lids gives a pixel difference under 0.5% (this checks the hinge sign).
- Game:
  - In calm, U.uGun.value.x < 0.05.
  - Force waves.state = 'fight' and step(1.5): > 0.95.
  - Fire to port, step(0.1): __game.looks.gunOffset(player.ship, 'port', 0) > 0.3 m.
  - After step(reload + 0.2): < 0.05.
- Frozen raider within 1 km: lids open on both sides.

proposals.title: A raider captain's ship that looks menacing: black iron, crimson crystals, red eyes and a swallow-tailed banner
proposals.chris_sees:
The raider captain's ship stands out from across the sky:
- black sails edged in a crimson stripe
- blackened iron fittings with gold trim
- crystals that burn crimson with crimson sparks
- red lanterns, and two red glowing eyes at her bow
- a big black-and-crimson swallow-tailed banner streaming from her mainmast
- a crimson-violet wake
proposals.why: Every fifth wave is the captain, worth four times the shards. Today she differs only in her black sails and gold pennant. Making her look like the leader gives the wave a centrepiece, at no cost while it runs.
proposals.how:
1. **raiders.js raiderArt(art, captain) (L53-60), for captains also clone:**
   - brass: color 0x2c2a2e, metalness 0.9, roughness 0.32 (black iron); band stays gold, so it reads as gold trim
   - bronze: 0x3b2d27
   - gem: emissive 0xff3a5a
   - crystal: emissive 0xff2448
   - canvas.userData.stripe = [0.55, 0.05, 0.08, 0.12]: SAIL_WEAR_FRAG mixes in the stripe colour where vEdge < 0.12 (the free edge), and every per-raider clone copies the plain array
2. **template() (L100-108), for captains:**
   - recolour the 'glow' Points colour attribute the way recolourPennants does: crystal glows (kind 1 and orange) to (1, 0.18, 0.28); lanterns (kind 2) to (1, 0.28, 0.16)
   - give emberPoints' shader a uTint uniform in place of its fixed colours, set to crimson
3. **Banner:** buildShip(R, level, art, {banner: true}) → masts() (L301-377) calls a new banner() beside pennant() (L379-395) on the tallest mast:
   - length 0.55H, width 0.16H, n = 10 at middle and 3 at far
   - the last 30% splits into two tails
   - vertex colours: black (0.06, 0.05, 0.06) with a crimson border
   - a billow attribute, so the existing flag shader flies it
4. **Eyes:** with {banner: true}, push two glows at the bow face: (±0.45·half(zb − 0.2), rim(zb) − 0.35·railScale, zb − 0.2), flicker kind, 0xff2a1a, size 0.9·L/25.
5. **Wake:** 0xff3070 (aether-wakes).
6. Build captain templates ahead with the existing raiders.prepare.
7. Docs: update docs/ships.md L39 and the raiders section in docs/game.md.
proposals.phone_cost:
- Nothing while running: every change is made once per template.
- About 40 triangles for the banner at middle, 12 at far.
- 2 more glow points.
- Same programs: colours aren't part of a program's key.
proposals.test:
- raiders.templates['brig:captain'].mid: the brass material's colour.getHex() is 0x2c2a2e, and no 'glow' colour is the orange 0xff9a2a.
- Its 'flag' mesh has more triangles than the crew version's by 30 to 50.
- Spawning a captain after a crew Brig adds 0 programs.
- A close-up picture through tools/closeups.mjs.

proposals.title: The Man-o'-war's crystal columns as glowing weak points that blow out one by one
proposals.chris_sees: The Man-o'-war's five crystal columns burn brighter than any other ship's and pulse slowly like a heartbeat. When he locks on to her, they glow gold at their edges, and the banner says to shoot her crystal columns to bring her down. Putting the crosshair on a column aims the guns at that column, and the crosshair turns gold. Each column dims and cracks as it is hit. When one gives out it bursts in a shower of gold and violet sparks, goes dark and smokes, and the fortress dips at that end.
proposals.why: She is a fortress with 7,000 hull, but only 2,600 crystals, and those sit in five small columns. Showing them gives the hardest fight a plan to follow and a series of big moments, with no change to her numbers.
proposals.how:
1. Reuses the per-column state from dying-crystals (uCrys and uCrack by cluster index from firstHit's idx).
2. **Template-level, for 'manowar':**
   - crystal glow sizes ×1.25
   - a uBeat uniform on the glow ShaderMaterial (k *= 0.85 + 0.25·pow(sin(3.5t), 8) when uBeat = 1)
3. **Lock highlight:**
   - main.js placeCamera, where locked is set: ease locked.ship.U.uMark toward 1 when locked.id === 'manowar', and toward 0 for any other
   - GEM_WEAR_FRAG adds (1, 0.86, 0.5)·uMark·pow(1 − |dot(normal, viewDir)|, 2)·(0.6 + 0.4·sin(6t))
   - glow k *= 1 + 0.4·uMark
4. **Column aim, in main.js aimFor:**
   - if locked.id === 'manowar', for each live column: c = centre of zones.crystals[i] × body.matrixWorld
   - if the angle between cam.look and (c − camera) is below atan(1.8·column radius / distance), aimPoint = intercept(muzzle, …, c, …) instead of locked.f.aimAt()
   - #aim gets the class 'weak' (gold)
5. **Blow-out, in looks.hit** when col_i crosses 0, once:
   - bolts.burst at c: 0xffe08a, 50 sparks, power 1.8; plus a 0xb25cff burst
   - uCrys_i = 0
   - smokeFrom emits from dead columns every 0.25 s
   - trim += 0.035·(z_i / (L/2)), eased into opts.trim; shipMotion adds it to body.rotation.x at L108
6. **Banner line,** in waves() where the wave title is chosen: add ' · shoot her glowing crystal columns to bring her down' when the wave has a Man-o'-war.
7. **Balance:** sim-fight aims at f.aimAt, so the sim's numbers stay the same; only a real Captain gains. Check by playing wave 12, run `node tools/sim-fight.mjs frigate 12 cross 12` for the record, and note it in docs/game.md "How hard it is".
proposals.phone_cost:
- A few uniforms.
- 5 angle tests a frame while locked on a Man-o'-war.
- One burst per blow-out (5 at most per Man-o'-war).
- No triangles or draw calls.
proposals.test:
- Spawn a frozen Man-o'-war 400 m off; hit column 2's box with share + 1 damage. Then:
  - a 'blowout' is counted once
  - U.uCrys[2] == 0, the others == 1
  - after step(2), body.rotation.x has moved in the direction set by the sign of z_2
- Point the camera at column 2's centre with the lock on: the aim point is within 3 m of that column, and #aim has the 'weak' class.

proposals.title: The treasure Galleon glints with gold, carries open chests, bleeds gold when hit and strikes her colours
proposals.chris_sees:
The treasure ship's fittings are bright gold:
- glints flash and twinkle across her rails and stern castle
- open chests heaped with gold sit on her deck
- hits on her hull throw a spray of gold glitter
- she leaves a glittering gold wake as she runs
- when she gives up, her pennants come down
proposals.why: She is the prize: 300 shards, and the 'shoot her sails' chase. Making her look rich makes the chase worth it, and the glints and gold wake help him keep her in sight as she runs.
proposals.how:
1. **Template-level, for 'galleon'** (a 'treasure' variant of raiderArt):
   - brass: 0xffcf4a, metalness 1, roughness 0.2
   - bronze: 0xc8953a
   - band emissiveIntensity 0.12
2. **Glints:**
   - buildShip opts.glints = 36: after batch.build(), sample merged 'brass' and 'rigMetal' vertices with y > deckY(z) + 0.3, or on the castle (z < quarterdeck.front), with a fixed stride
   - glows.push({p, size: 0.9·tileScale, color: 0xfff1c0, glint: true}); in glowPoints (build.js L67-99) these get kind 3
   - vertex: k = pow(max(0, sin(0.8t + 5.3·ph)), 48)·2.4 (each flashes about every 8 s, for about 0.15 s)
   - fragment: pass vKind; for kind 3 draw a four-point star: max(exp(−28|d.x|)·exp(−3|d.y|), the same with x and y swapped)
3. **Chests:** a new R.treasure in src/ships/galleon.js, e.g. [[-2.6, -9.5], [2.6, -1.4], [0, 6.2], [-5.0, 3.8], [5.0, -12.0], [-4.6, -5.2]], next to the hatches.
   - deckworks (parts.js L508) builds them at middle as well, before the `if (!q.cargo) return` at L579
   - each: a wood box 1.2 × 0.7 × 0.8, a gold heap (lathe, 8 segments, in brass), and a propped lid (box): about 90 triangles
4. **Gold glitter:** in main.js hitTest's player branch, when h.r.role === 'prize' and the part is 'hull', also bolts.burst(at, 0xffd54a, 10, 0.6).
5. **Striking her colours:** when f.down.why === 'struck', looks ramps U.uWind.y to 1 over 1.5 s. The flag shader collapses each pennant toward its hoist (transformed.z = mix(transformed.z, hoistZ, strike)) and lowers it 2 m.
6. **Wake:** gold glitter (aether-wakes).
proposals.phone_cost:
- 36 glint points inside the existing glow batch: no draw call.
- Treasure: about 540 triangles at middle (35,726 → about 36,300, inside the budget).
- The colours are set once per template.
- One small burst per hull hit on her only.
proposals.test:
- raiders.templates.galleon.mid's 'glow' geometry has at least 30 points of kind 3.
- The middle Galleon stays within 10,000-50,000 triangles.
- Force f.down = {why: 'struck', t: 0}, then step(2): U.uWind.value.y == 1.
- Spawning a Galleon adds 0 programs.

proposals.title: The crew patch her up between waves: holes become patches, fires go out, and she is new again in port
proposals.chris_sees: Between waves, as the bars fill back up, the fires and embers go out, the scorch marks shrink, and the sail holes close into darker stitched patches. The crystal cracks fade. Back in port his ship is spotless again.
proposals.why: The scars tell the story of the voyage. The patches show the repairs he is already being given (player.repair in waves()), and the port garage needs a clean ship.
proposals.how:
1. **looks.repair(k),** called right after player.repair(dt·0.12) in main.js waves():
   - all uHeat → 0
   - each scar's r scales by the healed fraction of the hull
   - each hole's radius moves toward −0.8·r: negative means 'patched'
   - uCrack eases down with each column's d_i (dying-crystals)
2. **SAIL_WEAR_FRAG:** for h.w < 0, don't discard. Draw a squarer patch:
   - max(|dx|, |dy|) in the sail's plane, using vLocal projected on the triangle's axes
   - diffuse × 0.82 inside
   - a stitched edge: step on fract(edge·12) darkening 0.6 along the border
3. **looks.reset(ship):** called in sail() before the voyage and in endVoyage → port.setMode('port'). It clears scars, holes and columns, and sets fold to 0 and lids closed.
4. Raiders never repair.
proposals.phone_cost: Nothing extra: the same loop with one more branch on a sign.
proposals.test:
- Damage the player's sails and hull with looks.hit, then set waves.state = 'choose' and step(25): every uHole.w < 0 and every uHeat == 0.
- endVoyage(1), then sail again: U.uScar is all zeros.
- A pixel check in port, before and after a voyage, shows no difference above 0.5%.
